doc.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998

title: The integrated band at Kelly's Stables and lost friends
summary: He played in an early integrated band at Kelly's Stables and mourns bandmates from Benny Carter and Erskine Hawkins who have died.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: The next band was organized by one of Benny Goodman’s saxophone players called Jerry Jerome. And he’s still living God rest his — he’s almost 90 years old, he’s living in the south somewhere. But myself, John Simmons on bass, I can’t think of the piano player’s name, and Arthur Herbert on drums, we were the first band, integrated band to play at Kelly’s Stables on 52nd Street. And one night, a great pianist named Nat Jaffe, said, “Hey man, this is one heck of a band, why don’t we keep this thing together?” And we kept it together until everybody went their own ways. And I’ve looked up, I’ve tried to find out whatever happened to Nat Jaffe, but I think he must have passed away I think way back in the forties. And you see when you talk about the forties and fifties, sometimes you have to bring in subjects like racial segregation and things like that, which is, you try to stay away from that even in conversations, because we’ve solved some of our problems, you know what I mean? And this is still the greatest country in the world, but we’ve solved most of our social problems and maybe I’m happy to have gone through them. You know what I mean? We’ve been through a lot of different places and segregated, especially during the time of the Benny Carter band. We were on tour, and this was in 1941, and this was one of the great bands with the Parrish brothers, myself, Lincoln Mills. Most of them are dead. I think maybe the sad part of my life would be that most of all of my friends have passed away. The Erskine Hawkins band, they’re all gone. There’s only one, two, three — about three of us, four of us, Johnny Grimes, great trumpet player; Doris Rollin, one of the singers, then Erskine passed away about three years ago himself, and Jimmy Harris, the trumpet player, a fine trumpet player, and all of the Count Basie band, all of the Duke Ellington band and most of them have left this planet. They’ve left me here, maybe sometimes I could tell a lot of lies. I could tell a lot of lies if I wanted to. But I’d like to tell things that actually, really happened to them.
